_note: Fictional phones. No summary scores are shown: only spec-sheet terms and lab measurements, written in mixed units on purpose (minutes vs hours, GB vs TB vs MB, millions vs lakhs; lower lux and lower f-numbers are better; a larger sensor has a smaller second number). Each main set has 1 correct phone (rank 1), 1 main trap (rank 2), 1 second trap (rank 3) and 1 dominated phone (rank 4). The correct phone is the best phone within budget on the card's Priority 1, decided by the lab measurement in '_truth' (hidden from the browser). The main trap is better on Priority 2 and has flashier headline specs, so it is a real trade-off. The second trap is over budget. The dominated phone is worse than the correct phone on every measured value and costs the same or more. tests/test_phone_sets.py checks all of this. Card positions are shuffled per participant. Shopping screen: each card shows a picture, the colours, the price and the start of the specs; 'View details' opens the full spec rows, which include the measured values (in mixed units). The 'details' and 'review' entries are shown only on the 'change your choice?' screen after the round. Picture styles ('look') are counterbalanced so each role gets each style once across S1-S4.

card.text: Buy the phone with the most storage.

phones.name: Alpha One

specs.camera: 50 MP · low light: sharp photos down to 9 lux

phones.review: A plain everyday phone. Fine for calls, chat and video.

specs.camera: 50 MP · low light: sharp photos down to 8 lux

phones.review: Light, with a smooth 120 Hz screen.

phones.name: Gamma Plus

specs.camera: 64 MP · low light: sharp photos down to 7 lux

phones.review: Huge storage for photos and videos.

phones.name: Delta Go

specs.camera: 48 MP · low light: sharp photos down to 12 lux

phones.review: The cheapest option here. Basic but works.

card.persona: Your younger sibling is starting college and will be out of the hostel from morning to night.
card.text: Budget: up to ₹25,000. Priority 1: the battery must last the whole long day. Priority 2: good photos indoors and at night. Not needed: gaming.

phones.name: Nova X2

specs.camera: 50 MP, 1/1.56" sensor, f/1.8, OIS · low light: sharp photos down to 4 lux

phones.review: Still had charge left at night in our day-long test. Indoor photos are good, though very dark scenes get a little soft.

phones.name: Zen 5 Max

specs.camera: 108 MP, 1/1.4" sensor, f/1.7, OIS · low light: sharp photos down to 2 lux

phones.review: A big 6000 mAh battery and a large, bright camera sensor that shines at night. The 144 Hz LCD screen is very smooth to scroll.

phones.name: Volt Pro

specs.camera: 64 MP, 1/1.5" sensor, f/1.8, OIS · low light: sharp photos down to 3 lux

phones.review: A flagship-class processor that flies through games. Good night photos; the battery is average.

phones.name: Pixa 4

specs.camera: 50 MP, 1/2.8" sensor, f/2.0 · low light: sharp photos down to 10 lux

phones.review: Simple and dependable for calls, chat and social media. Photos are fine in daylight.

card.persona: Your aunt wants to photograph her grandchildren on stage at school functions, sitting far back in the audience, and she uses her phone a lot outdoors.
card.text: Budget: up to ₹30,000. Priority 1: a camera that zooms in clearly from far away. Priority 2: a screen that is easy to see in bright sunlight.

phones.name: Lumo C7

specs.camera: 50 MP main + 50 MP telephoto (3× optical), OIS · zoom: faces stay sharp up to 6×

phones.review: The telephoto lens brings far-away subjects close. The screen is pleasant indoors; in strong sun you may need to shade it.

phones.name: Orbit 200

specs.camera: 200 MP main, 100× digital zoom · zoom: faces stay sharp up to 2×

phones.review: A huge 200 MP camera with up to 100× zoom on the spec sheet, and a very bright screen that stays readable outside.

phones.name: Kite S

specs.camera: 50 MP main + 50 MP telephoto (3× optical), OIS · zoom: faces stay sharp up to 5×

phones.review: Excellent zoom and a dazzling screen in a premium design.

phones.name: Echo 9

specs.camera: 64 MP main, 10× digital zoom · zoom: faces stay sharp up to 1.5×

phones.review: A solid everyday phone with a 64 MP camera and digital zoom.

card.persona: Your cousin travels home by train every weekend with no internet on the way, and downloads many movies before leaving.
card.text: Budget: up to ₹22,000. Priority 1: as much free space as possible for downloaded movies. Priority 2: a good screen for watching them.

phones.name: Aero 3

specs.display: 6.6" IPS LCD, 90 Hz · peak brightness 600 nits
specs.storage: 6 GB / 256 GB · 228 GB free out of the box

details: Free space out of the box
phones.review: Lots of room for downloads. The LCD screen is clear indoors but not as vivid as AMOLED.

phones.name: Glide 6 Plus

specs.storage: 8 GB + 8 GB virtual RAM (16 GB*) / 128 GB · 0.1 TB free out of the box

details: Free space out of the box
phones.review: A gorgeous AMOLED screen that is great for movies, and '16 GB RAM' for smooth multitasking.

phones.name: Spark 12

specs.camera: 50 MP, OIS
specs.storage: 8 GB / 256 GB · 0.23 TB free out of the box

details: Free space out of the box
phones.review: Big storage and a beautiful screen, in a slim body.

phones.name: Mira 2

specs.storage: 6 GB / 128 GB · 98,000 MB free out of the box

details: Free space out of the box
phones.review: Basic phone with a standard screen and storage.

card.persona: Your friend plays long online games (2 hours or more) every evening.
card.text: Budget: up to ₹28,000. Priority 1: games must stay smooth for the whole long session, not just at the start. Priority 2: battery life while gaming.

phones.name: Volt 7

specs.chip: Snapdragon 7+ Gen 3 (4 nm), vapour-chamber cooling · AnTuTu 1.32 million (first run) · after 30 min of gaming: keeps 88% of its speed
specs.camera: 50 MP, OIS

phones.review: Stays cool and steady in long matches. Battery while gaming is average.

phones.name: Titan GT

specs.chip: Dimensity 8300 (4 nm), 'Gaming Mode' · AnTuTu 14,50,000 (first run) · after 30 min of gaming: drops to 0.61× of its speed
specs.camera: 64 MP

phones.review: Very fast out of the box, with a 165 Hz screen, 16 GB RAM and a big 6000 mAh battery that lasts through long gaming.

phones.name: Nova Ultra

specs.chip: Snapdragon 8s Gen 3 (4 nm) · AnTuTu 1.6 million (first run) · after 30 min of gaming: keeps 80% of its speed
specs.camera: 50 MP, OIS

phones.review: Top speed and strong battery, at a higher price.

phones.name: Pulse 5

specs.chip: Dimensity 7050 (6 nm) · AnTuTu 6,80,000 (first run) · after 30 min of gaming: keeps 70% of its speed
specs.camera: 64 MP

phones.review: A decent all-rounder for casual games.

card.persona: Your grandparent forgets to charge their phone and keeps many family videos on it.
card.text: Budget: up to ₹20,000. Priority 1: battery life. Priority 2: plenty of free storage.
